- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.1) — model underreacts to bearish sentiment.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes or drops.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects downward — overshoots by 2–5% in the following 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently forecasts prices to stay high after a peak, ignoring short-term volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile.
- When sentiment is consistently negative, model underestimates the depth of the correction — fails to account for sharp downside moves.
- Model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from negative to positive, leading to delayed price recovery.
